item.text:
**8B.10 Research Note: Félix Tshisekedi (2024)**

**Bottom line:** mixed, but only *modestly* closer to parts of his program by year-end. There were real short-term gains in cabinet formation, macro stabilization, technocratic staffing, and ceasefire diplomacy. But the gains were fragile, security conditions stayed bad, repression remained severe, and the late-2024 constitutional-term-limit push cut against a clean “progress toward the stated program” reading.

### Claim-Level Evidence

- **IMF Executive Board Concludes 2024 Article IV Consultation and Sixth ECF Review**
  - **Publisher:** IMF
  - **Date:** 2024-07-03
  - **URL:** https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/03/pr24253-drc-imf-exec-board-concludes-2024-art-iv-consult-completes-6th-rev-ecf-arr
  - **Claim:** The IMF said the DRC maintained prudent macro policies, avoided monetary financing, improved revenue mobilization, and built reserves, while also warning that reforms were slow and the security crisis in the east was weighing on the economy.
  - **Maps to:** 8B.10

- **DR Congo president appoints country’s first female prime minister**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** 2024-04-01
  - **URL:** https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-president-appoints-countrys-first-female-prime-minister-2024-04-01/
  - **Claim:** Tshisekedi ended post-election uncertainty by naming Judith Suminwa, a technocratic planning minister, as prime minister after coalition bargaining.
  - **Maps to:** 8B.10, and directly informs 4B.1 / 6B.2 where relevant

- **Madame Judith SUMINWA TULUKA, nommée Première Ministre**
  - **Publisher:** Ministère de la Communication et Médias
  - **Date:** 2024-04-01
  - **URL:** https://communication.gouv.cd/actualites/communications-du-gouvernement/18/madame-judith-suminwa-tuluka-nommee-premiere-ministre-de-la-republique-democratique-du-congo
  - **Claim:** The presidency explicitly framed Suminwa’s appointment as competence-based and tied to socio-economic development planning.
  - **Maps to:** 8B.10

- **Democratic Republic of the Congo - April 2024**
  - **Publisher:** International IDEA
  - **Date:** 2024-04
  - **URL:** https://www.idea.int/democracytracker/report/democratic-republic-congo/april-2024
  - **Claim:** The appointment of the first female prime minister was treated as a meaningful inclusion signal and a partial fulfillment of a campaign promise on gender equality.
  - **Maps to:** 8B.10

- **Collective effort essential to get DR Congo on firm path to peace**
  - **Publisher:** UN Office at Geneva
  - **Date:** 2024-09-30
  - **URL:** https://www.ungeneva.org/en/news-media/news/2024/09/98156/collective-effort-essential-get-dr-congo-firm-path-peace
  - **Claim:** The UN said fighting had notably decreased after the 30 July ceasefire and that an active DRC-Rwanda dialogue framework was operating under Angolan mediation, but also stressed that peace was not yet won.
  - **Maps to:** 8B.10

- **Army disarray hobbles Congo’s fight with Rwanda-backed rebels, officers say**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** 2024-07-04
  - **URL:** https://www.straitstimes.com/world/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say
  - **Claim:** Reuters described severe army disarray, weak logistics, poor discipline, and reliance on poorly controlled proxy militias; Tshisekedi also threatened to declare war against Rwanda, showing escalation pressure alongside insecurity.
  - **Maps to:** 8B.10

- **Congolese president sacks military top brass in major reshuffle**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** 2024-12-20
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/congolese-president-sacks-military-top-brass-in-major-reshuffle/2411531/
  - **Claim:** Tshisekedi replaced the armed forces chief, military intelligence head, and many senior officers in a major late-year reshuffle, which can be read as corrective reorganization but also as damage control after serious failures.
  - **Maps to:** 8B.10

- **Tshisekedi backed the Court of Accounts’ control function**
  - **Publisher:** Présidence RDC
  - **Date:** 2024-10-07
  - **URL:** https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_chef_de_l_etat_a_assiste_a_louverture_de_la_session_extraordinaire_du_conseil_superieur_de_la_cour_des_comptes
  - **Claim:** The presidency publicly backed the Court of Accounts’ oversight role, and the court said that support helped revive anti-corruption control and public-finance oversight.
  - **Maps to:** 8B.10

- **DR Congo: World Report 2024**
  - **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch
  - **Date:** 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/democratic-republic-congo
  - **Claim:** HRW said repression of journalists, activists, critics, and opposition members continued, security forces committed serious abuses, and the administration made little progress on systemic reforms.
  - **Maps to:** 8B.10

- **DR Congo President Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations**
  - **Publisher:** Amnesty International
  - **Date:** 2024-09-30
  - **URL:** https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/
  - **Claim:** Amnesty said the state of siege militarized everyday life, concentrated power in military and police officials, and coincided with a crackdown on dissent; it also said the government failed to prevent and punish major abuses.
  - **Maps to:** 8B.10

- **Congo lifts moratorium on death penalty, justice ministry circular shows**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** 2024-03-15
  - **URL:** https://www.yahoo.com/news/congo-lifts-moratorium-death-penalty-153836346.html
  - **Claim:** The government lifted the death-penalty moratorium to rid the army of “traitors” and curb terrorism and banditry, a hardline discipline move that also signaled rights regression.
  - **Maps to:** 8B.10

- **Congo and Rwanda say peace talks in Angola will not take place**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** 2024-12-15
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/congo-and-rwanda-say-peace-talks-in-angola-will-not-take-place/2404370/
  - **Claim:** The planned Angola summit collapsed after deadlock over direct DRC-M23 dialogue, dashing hopes of a durable peace deal by year-end.
  - **Maps to:** 8B.10

- **Fighting resumes in eastern Congo, army and M23 say**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** 2024-12-03
  - **URL:** https://www.yahoo.com/news/fighting-resumes-eastern-congo-army-100023151.html
  - **Claim:** Fighting resumed in eastern Congo in violation of the ceasefire, showing that the de-escalation framework was not holding by late 2024.
  - **Maps to:** 8B.10

### Synthesis

- **What improved:** Tshisekedi made some concrete progress toward his governing program in 2024: he formed a cabinet after coalition delay, installed technocratic ministers, backed an IMF-backed stabilization track, and kept diplomacy alive on the eastern conflict.
- **What did not:** the east remained highly unstable, coercive security practices persisted, public freedoms stayed under pressure, and the late-2024 constitutional revision push made the power-consolidation reading stronger, not weaker.
- **Durability test:** the best positive signals were either partial, reversible, or executive-centered. The strongest negative signals were structural and persistent.

**Specific search gap:** I found no reliable evidence that 2024 produced a durable settlement in the east or a broad improvement in rights and rule-of-law conditions. The strongest positive evidence is temporary ceasefire reduction and macro stabilization; the strongest counterevidence is renewed fighting, collapsed peace talks, repression, and term-limit maneuvering.
